notes.title: Ergastulum: Dungeon Nightmares III Out on Early Access
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/9861420/0e23f5f039210b49c7febe1b2e57848522bab7f3.png[/img]

The new chapter of Dungeon Nightmares is open to players on Early Access.

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/598430/Ergastulum_Dungeon_Nightmares_III/]Ergastulum: Dungeon Nightmares III[/url] has been a 3-4 year journey to get here and I hope what I have created delivers :)

At Early Access launch, there will be Acts 1 & 2. Additional Acts, enemies and story will be added with regular updates but the main focus is to give you a chance to experience this new horror I have created.

Please pop over there to take a peek... looking forward in hearing your feedback.

notes.title: Ergastulum Dev Updates
notes.content:
[h1]Welcome Isserley to the Ergastulum Project[/h1]
I want to start off by welcoming [b]Isserley[/b] to the [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/598430/Ergastulum/]Ergastulum[/url] project. Isserley is going to be composing the original score, which will comprise of Industrial noisiness, ambience and even a little classical! Here is a short blurb from her own mouth.

[quote=Isserley]I've played the beta a whole bunch and you're in for a real treat, as long as you consider being on edge for hours on end a treat[/quote]

And from what she has produced so far, this game is not only going to be a real hellish treat for your eyes but also for your ears. Stay tuned for more updates soon and make sure to check out her [url=https://www.facebook.com/IsserleyIsHome/posts/593710910963181]Facebook[/url] page.

[h1]Even More Enemies?!?[/h1]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/hEzzxHe.gif[/img]

In other news, I recently created something that was inspired by an old movie called Salem's Lot.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/D7uApEb.png[/img]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/Y2O2Kdm.png[/img]

For those that have seen it may remember THAT window scene.

notes.title: Dungeon Nightmares Difficulty
notes.content:
I was curious about what players felt about the challenge my games bring (mainly the Dungeon Nightmares difficulty).

When I was making the sequel, the game was a lot easier (in my mind) but during the final weeks of development, I made the choice to make it harder, more challenging, and stay true to itself. I still firmly believe that this was the right decision.

However, as I in the process of designing my next game (unannounced) I wanted to through a quick poll out there about difficulty.

Here are the results of the poll on Twitter after 24 hours:

[list]
[*]33% Make it harder, I'm crazy
[*][b]44% Don't change a thing[/b]
[*]23% Too much of a nightmare
[/list]

The results seem to agree with my original feelings that players like the challenge my games bring. However, feel free to keep discussing this here or in the forums here :)

http://steamcommunity.com/app/382090/discussions/0/365163686059386194/

notes.title: One Week On...
notes.content:
It's been just over a week since releasing Dungeon Nightmares II on Steam and I am happy to see players enjoying the game.

Since the release, I have been fixing a few bugs and adjusting a few difficult areas of the game. [b]Patch 1.02[/b] that was released today also updates the game to include a new Options area on the Main Menu where you can adjust a few controls settings and toggle V-Sync.

So what next for [b]Dungeon Nightmares[/b]? I don't know. I have a few ideas that I want to do... maybe a small treat for fans around Halloween :) but lets see how things go!

After that, I want to go back to my [b]Oculus Rift[/b] and get some stuff done. That will be exciting.

Lastly, thank you to everyone that bought the game.
